what_it_does: This layer turns positions, sensor detections and reports into a shared, map-based picture that people and machines can act on. It comprises (1) foundation geospatial data (basemaps, imagery, elevation/3D terrain, feature data, symbology standards such as MIL-STD-2525), (2) position reporting and blue-force tracking (BFT) that publishes own-force locations over radios/SATCOM, (3) track management that ingests detections from radars, EO/IR, RF, and data links, correlates/deduplicates them into single tracks with identity (friend/hostile/unknown) and track-quality, (4) the common operational picture (COP) application that fuses those layers with overlays (graphics, control measures, geofences, airspace) and lets operators annotate, chat and task, and (5) the plumbing that synchronizes all of the above across servers, radios and edge devices in disconnected, degraded, intermittent and limited (DDIL) conditions. In the U.S. force the dismounted/tactical COP is dominated by the government-owned Team Awareness Kit (TAK: ATAK/WinTAK/iTAK/TAK Server), the mounted COP by JBC-P/Mounted Mission Command, the air-and-missile-defense track picture by IBCS/CEC/Aegis/Link 16, and the theater/joint picture increasingly by Palantir (Maven Smart System) and Anduril (Lattice, NGC2 data layer).

sub_taxonomy.name: Foundation geospatial data and services
sub_taxonomy.note: Basemaps, imagery, elevation, 3D terrain/3D Tiles, feature data, map production and serving (NGA, Army Geospatial Center, Esri, Vantor/Maxar, Cesium/Bentley, One World Terrain). Largely commoditized at the data layer by NGA/commercial contracts; differentiation lies in currency, resolution, 3D, and delivery to the edge.

sub_taxonomy.name: Blue-force tracking and position reporting
sub_taxonomy.note: JBC-P/MMC over BFT-2 L-band SATCOM and terrestrial radios; ATAK over Nett Warrior/MANET/mesh (goTenna, Somewear, Persistent Systems). Includes GPS-denied position integrity, which overlaps the PNT segment.

sub_taxonomy.name: Track management and correlation (air/missile/maritime)
sub_taxonomy.note: IBCS, FAAD C2, Aegis, CEC, Link 16 / JREAP, JTMC. Fire-control-quality tracks, dual-track resolution, track identity. Historically prime-dominated and classified; highest technical bar.

sub_taxonomy.name: COP applications and clients
sub_taxonomy.note: TAK family (government-owned, free), JBC-P/MMC-S, CPCE, SitaWare, Palantir Gotham/Maven, Anduril Lattice, Immersive Wisdom. Commoditizing at the basic map-and-icons level; value migrating to data layers and workflow/plugins.

sub_taxonomy.name: Sensor-to-map workflows and overlays
sub_taxonomy.note: Georegistration of drone/ISR video to maps, rapid 3D reconstruction at the edge (Reveal Farsight), automated change detection (Vantor Luno B), c-UAS sensor tracks onto the tactical map (FAAD C2, Lattice), overlays/geofences/airspace measures (TAIS/ADAM cell).

sub_taxonomy.name: DDIL synchronization and offline geospatial
sub_taxonomy.note: TAK Server federation, offline tile packages (MBTiles/GeoPackage), delta sync of overlays, low/no-bandwidth collaboration (Immersive Wisdom), edge-to-cloud data mesh (NGC2). This is where founders report the most manual workaround today (INFERENCE).

sub_taxonomy.name: Coalition/partner COP federation and releasability
sub_taxonomy.note: Mission Partner Environment, ASCA, NATO standards (APP-6, ADatP-3, JC3IEDM/NVG), TAK federation across national servers, Ukraine Delta. Heavy on security/cross-domain accreditation.

current_architecture.description: A layered but fragmented architecture. At the dismounted/tactical edge, ATAK on Android end-user devices exchanges Cursor-on-Target (CoT) messages peer-to-peer or through TAK Server (federated, TLS, with mission packages and data sync). Mounted forces use JBC-P/Mounted Mission Command on Leonardo DRS MFoCS hardware with Viasat BFT-2 L-band SATCOM transport, being modernized under MMC-S (software) and MMC-T (transport). Command posts use CPCE and, in the NGC2 divisions, an Anduril Lattice / Palantir Foundry edge-to-cloud data mesh with third-party applications. Air and missile defense runs fire-control-quality track management on IBCS (Army), Aegis/CEC (Navy), FAAD C2 (c-UAS/SHORAD) connected via Link 16/JREAP and, experimentally, JTMC. Foundation data flows from NGA (Map of the World, commercial imagery via Luno/EOCL), Army Geospatial Center, One World Terrain (3D Tiles/Cesium) and Esri ArcGIS servers, typically pre-packaged to the edge as MBTiles/GeoPackage/KMZ. Theater/joint COPs increasingly use Palantir Maven Smart System. Interoperability between these stacks depends on translation gateways and standards (CoT, VMF, Link 16 J-series, ASCA, NATO NVG/APP-6), and in practice on liaison officers and manual re-entry (INFERENCE).

current_architecture.security_domain: Spans unclassified (ATAK-CIV, DHS/CBP, training), CUI/IL4-IL5 (most TAK-MIL and JBC-P traffic, mission data), SECRET (CPCE, Link 16, IBCS/Aegis, NGC2 division data, coalition MPE enclaves) and TS/SCI (NGA/Maven at IC level). Cross-domain movement of tracks and overlays requires accredited cross-domain solutions.
current_architecture.connectivity_dependency: High. BFT-2 depends on L-band SATCOM; ATAK depends on MANET/mesh/cellular or SATCOM to reach TAK Server; NGC2 data mesh assumes intermittent links with edge nodes; track management for air defense demands low-latency dedicated links (IFCN, Link 16, CEC DDS).
current_architecture.what_breaks_when_disconnected: Positions go stale and units disappear from the COP; overlays and mission packages diverge between servers and devices; imagery/3D terrain not pre-cached cannot be viewed; duplicate or conflicting tracks persist because correlation requires shared history; chat and tasking revert to voice; on reconnection, bulk resync saturates the link (INFERENCE from architecture; low-bandwidth pain acknowledged by USAF sole-source purchase of Immersive Wisdom and by Bold Quest network-limitation reporting).

technical_difficulty.summary: Basic COP functionality (map, icons, chat, overlays) is a solved, commoditized problem: TAK provides it free with source available, and Esri/Cesium provide the GIS and 3D substrate. The hard problems are (a) fire-control-quality multi-sensor track correlation with identity under latency and adversarial conditions, (b) keeping many devices and servers consistent over DDIL links without flooding them, (c) scaling the picture to thousands of friendly and hostile small drones without operator overload, (d) coalition federation with releasability controls and cross-domain accreditation, and (e) integrating with legacy message standards (VMF, Link 16) whose specifications are controlled. Difficulty is medium for edge/DDIL data sync and plugin work, high for track correlation at fire-control quality and for cross-domain federation.
required_expertise: Geospatial engineering (projections, tiling, 3D Tiles, GeoPackage/MBTiles, symbology)
Distributed systems and CRDT/delta-sync for intermittent networks
Tactical networking (MANET, SATCOM budgets, TAK Server federation, radio integration)
Multi-target tracking and data association (Kalman/IMM, JPDA/MHT, track-to-track fusion)
Android/Kotlin and TAK SDK plugin development; TAKX/web front ends
Cybersecurity and ATO/RMF, STIGs, IL5/secret enclave practices
Message standards (CoT, VMF, Link 16 J-series, NATO STANAGs)
Computer vision/photogrammetry for sensor-to-map workflows (optional but valued)
technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Correlating and deduplicating tracks from heterogeneous, unsynchronized sensors (drones, c-UAS radars, BFT, Link 16) at the tactical edge with enough confidence to support fires or c-UAS engagement decisions, while degrading gracefully under DDIL and jamming. This sits between what TAK does (position sharing) and what IBCS/CEC do (fire-control networks) and is currently done by liaison officers, JICOs and vendor-specific fusion (Lattice) rather than an open layer.
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: Map rendering (Mapbox/MapLibre, Cesium), basemap/imagery supply (NGA, Vantor, Planet), the COP client itself (ATAK/WinTAK/TAKX), TAK Server, symbology libraries, tile packaging, chat/messaging, GPS position reporting, cloud hosting at IL5.

capital_intensity.assumptions: Software-only product built as ATAK/TAKX plugin or TAK Server-side service using ATAK-CIV, public TAK Server source and commercial/open imagery; two founders plus 2-4 engineers; demo cost includes SBIR/OTA cycles, a government sponsor for TAK-MIL access, exercise participation (travel, hardware, radios), CUI-compliant infrastructure (NIST 800-171/CMMC) and a cleared advisor; production includes ATO/IL5 hosting, cybersecurity assessment, sustained engineering, integration with a PoR (NGC2 app ecosystem, MMC or SBMC), and 12-24 months of sales cycle. Hardware-inclusive plays (radios, edge compute) would double or triple these ranges. Track-correlation products aimed at fires/air defense need classified test venues and would exceed the top of these ranges.

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: yes - ATAK-CIV, TAK Server source, OpenStreetMap/commercial imagery, Cesium ion and public MIL-STD-2525 allow a full unclassified prototype; DHS/first-responder TAK users are an unclassified proving ground.
regulatory_access.government_data_required: For military relevance: TAK-MIL builds and plugin SDK (government sponsorship required), JBC-P/VMF and Link 16 message specs (controlled), operational position data (CUI or classified), exercise data. Realistic access comes only with a sponsor (SBIR TPOC, AAL, AFWERX, DIU) or via a prime/Anduril-NGC2 ecosystem partner.
regulatory_access.itar_ear: Commercial mapping software is generally EAR-controlled at low levels, but military-specific TAK-MIL plugins, Link 16/VMF implementations, fire-control track algorithms and anything designed for a defense article can fall under ITAR (USML Category XI/XXI) or 600-series ECCNs. Whether a specific product is ITAR-controlled requires a commodity jurisdiction analysis by export counsel; do not assume ATAK-CIV licensing extends to MIL features.
regulatory_access.cui_likely: Yes - almost any operational integration produces CUI; expect NIST SP 800-171 / CMMC Level 2 obligations early.
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: Likely for track management (IBCS/Link 16/CEC), NGC2 division data and coalition MPE; not necessarily for DDIL map/overlay sync or plugin businesses focused at CUI level or on DHS/allied civil users.
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: No for an unclassified TAK plugin MVP; yes (at least one cleared FSO/engineer and a facility clearance path) before production integration with secret-level systems.
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: A non-U.S.-person founder (Indonesian, not a permanent resident) cannot be given access to ITAR technical data or TAK-MIL export-controlled SDKs without a license or exemption, which are rarely granted for this use; a German founder gains U.S.-person status only upon permanent residency. SBIR/STTR eligibility requires the small business to be more than 50 percent owned and controlled by U.S. citizens or permanent residents, so cap-table structure matters. Facility clearance would raise FOCI mitigation questions if non-U.S. ownership or control is material. All of this needs specialist export-control and government-contracts counsel; this file describes the constraints, not a legal conclusion.

why_not_solved.explanation: The basic COP (map, positions, overlays, chat) is solved by government-owned TAK at zero license cost, which removes the commercial market for a new COP client. Any startup must sit on top of or beside TAK, not replace it.

TAK (TPC), mounted (PM MC), soldier-worn (PEO Soldier), division data layer (NGC2), air defense (PEO M&S), foundation data (NGA/AGC/PEO STRI) are separate buyers with separate money; no single office owns the end-to-end picture, as GAO-25-106454 documents at the joint level.

Fire-control track management lives inside IBCS, Aegis/CEC and FAAD C2, whose interfaces and message specs are controlled; Lattice and Foundry are becoming the division-level integration points, giving Anduril/Palantir gatekeeper power over what apps run in NGC2.
The most valuable track and coalition data is secret or higher, so unclassified startups cannot see the real problem until they have sponsors, clearances and enclaves.
Legacy standards (VMF, Link 16, ADatP-3), radio-specific transports and vendor-specific APIs make each integration bespoke; exercises still rely on translation gateways and liaison officers.
TAK plugin work is services-priced; the biggest TAK services house (PAR Government) sold to Booz Allen for a modest sum (RECALL), signaling limited venture-scale product margins in plugins.

Edge GPUs, on-device photogrammetry, CRDT-style sync and cheap commercial 3D terrain (OWT/3D Tiles) only recently made offline 3D and delta-sync practical on soldier devices, so DDIL data logistics is genuinely fresh ground.
Open, vendor-neutral track correlation for dense small-drone environments below the fire-control tier does not exist as a product; JTMC and IBCS address the high end, TAK the low end.

attractiveness.bull: The picture is being rebuilt around data layers (NGC2, Maven, Lattice) and around a free, ubiquitous client (TAK, 500k+ users, TAKX in 2026), which lowers distribution cost for anyone shipping a plugin or server-side service. Real money is moving now: $354M SBMC prototypes, roughly $200M of NGC2 OTAs with a June 2026 baseline decision, repeat OWT and Luno awards, and a five-year sole-source for low-bandwidth collaboration. Drone density and DDIL create new pain that legacy architectures were not designed for, and a two-person team can build a credible unclassified prototype on ATAK-CIV, TAK Server and commercial 3D data for well under $250k.
attractiveness.bear: The client and basemap layers are commoditized by the government itself; Anduril and Palantir now own the division-level integration points and can absorb any adjacent feature; track management at fire-control quality is classified, prime-dominated and beyond a seed-stage team; the buyer landscape is fragmented and slow; TAK plugin businesses are services-priced; and a non-U.S.-person co-founder cannot touch TAK-MIL SDKs or ITAR technical data without licenses. Prior small entrants mostly landed in SBIR/STRATFI or modest sole-source ceilings rather than programs of record.
attractiveness.verdict: Medium overall, with a bimodal split: low for a new COP client, basemap or generic plugin business; medium-to-high for a narrow software wedge in DDIL geospatial data logistics or dense-sensor track deduplication delivered as a TAK/TAKX-native service and positioned to plug into NGC2 and SBMC ecosystems. Not a fit for a two-person team without a U.S.-person technical lead and a government sponsor.

test/evaluation - DOT&E FY2023 assessment of MMC-S; CJADC2 minimum viable capability declared (RECALL)
repeat/production data buys - OWT Phase 4 (Mar), Luno A $290M (Sept); Booz Allen acquires PAR Government (RECALL)
prototype solicitation and awards - Luno B (Jan), GAO-25-106454 (Apr), SBMC RFS (Apr), NGC2 Anduril OTA $99.6M (Jul), Lockheed NGC2 (Sept), SBMC $354M (Sept), TAK 500k users and TAKX roadmap (Nov)

follow-on toward production - Vantor Luno B order (Feb), Vantor OWT up to $217M (Feb), Anduril selected to lead NGC2 common data layer baseline (Jun), PC-C6 (Jul), Anduril SBMC redesign (Aug), JIATF-401 c-sUAS guide (Sept)

market_stage.rationale: Foundation data and the TAK client are mature with repeat buys; the integrating data layer (NGC2) and soldier-worn device (SBMC) are moving from prototype to baseline/follow-on within 12-18 months of award, which is the transition phase. Track management for air defense is mature/production. The segment as a whole is therefore transitioning, with the consolidation point being who controls the division data layer and the TAKX ecosystem.

proto_purgatory.notes: Mixed. Small entrants show classic purgatory patterns: Reveal Technology went SBIR to STRATFI ($33.6M) without a visible program of record; Immersive Wisdom went SBIR to a sole-source ceiling contract and an MDA IDIQ slot; Edgybees and Danti remain in SBIR. Soldier-worn SA itself cycled seven years of IVAS prototypes before restarting as SBMC prototypes. Counter-examples exist: NGC2 moved from a July 2025 OTA to a June 2026 baseline selection, and OWT/Luno show repeat production-style buys, but those went to Anduril/Palantir and Vantor, not to seed-stage companies.
proto_purgatory.opportunity_or_warning: Warning for standalone small vendors selling to program offices; opportunity if the wedge rides an ecosystem that is already transitioning (NGC2 application layer, SBMC/ATAK plugins, TAKX migration) so the startup is pulled into a baseline rather than pushing its own program.

candidate_gaps.title: Open track deduplication and correlation for drone-dense tactical pictures below the fire-control tier
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Brigade-and-below COPs now receive overlapping detections of the same small drones from c-UAS radars, RF sensors, EO/IR, BFT and partner feeds, and no vendor-neutral layer correlates them into single, identified tracks with confidence before the operator is overloaded.
candidate_gaps.user: ADAM/BAE cell, battle captain, c-UAS operator at company through division; JICO at higher echelons.
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Each sensor or system publishes its own track/CoT to TAK Server, FAAD C2 or Lattice. 2) Operators see multiple icons for the same object with different IDs. 3) A human (often a liaison or JICO) decides which is real, deletes or merges by hand or via vendor-specific fusion. 4) Friendly drone flights are deconflicted through airspace control measures updated by broadcast, not by automated blue-drone tracking. 5) Engagement decisions wait for confirmation by voice.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: IBCS/JTMC (fire-control tier, heavy, classified), Anduril Lattice fusion (proprietary, tied to Anduril sensors and NGC2), FAAD C2 correlation (Northrop, limited to its sensor set), manual JICO management on Link 16.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Dual tracks and identity ambiguity multiply with sensor count; correlation logic is siloed in proprietary stacks; nothing runs at the edge in DDIL with open interfaces (CoT/TAK) and explainable confidence.

evidence.claim: Services pursue C2 projects in isolation without clear goals; cross-organizational issues unaddressed.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Friendly force tracking between ground and air remains inadequately integrated (fratricide risk).
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Industry (AeroVironment) argues 2026 drone swarms are being fought with Cold War C2 architecture; MWI notes deconfliction doctrine lags.
evidence.label: INFERENCE

evidence.label: FACT

evidence.label: FACT

evidence.label: INFERENCE

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Needs labeled multi-sensor track data that lives at CUI/secret level, sensor vendor cooperation, and a test venue with real drones and radars; validation requires exercises; incumbents keep correlation inside their products as a moat.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: High. Anduril can extend Lattice fusion to any sensor and now leads the NGC2 data layer; Northrop can extend FAAD C2. A startup wins only if it becomes the neutral, certified correlation service that program offices want to avoid vendor lock-in.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: A TAK-Server-side and TAKX plugin service that ingests CoT and c-UAS sensor feeds, performs track-to-track association with explainable confidence and blue-drone identity via Remote ID / flight-plan cross-referencing, and publishes merged tracks back over CoT; runs on an edge box in DDIL.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Ingest simulated and DHS/civil drone-detection feeds plus ATAK-CIV positions; demonstrate dedup rate, latency and false-merge metrics on a test range; publish as an open CoT extension.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Recorded multi-sensor drone detection data (initially civil/commercial c-UAS and Remote ID), later CUI exercise data via a sponsor.
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: TAK Server, CoT, FAAD C2 or Lattice interfaces (proprietary; require partnership), Link 16 gateway later.
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: Army xTech / AAL, AFWERX SBIR, DIU c-UAS solicitations, JIATF-401 demonstrations, DHS S&T (unclassified path).
candidate_gaps.why_now: Army intent to field very large numbers of small drones and the JIATF-401 stand-up create a track-density problem that did not exist in 2022; NGC2 is defining an application layer that third-party services could plug into.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Anduril/Northrop absorb the function inside NGC2/FAAD C2 before a startup gets an exercise slot; fires-adjacent correlation needs classified validation.

candidate_gaps.title: DDIL geospatial data logistics: delta-sync and prioritized distribution of basemaps, 3D terrain and overlays to the edge
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Units still pre-load maps and 3D terrain by hand and lose overlay consistency across devices and servers when links drop, because no fielded service versions, prioritizes and delta-syncs geospatial data across TAK Server federations and NGC2 edge nodes.
candidate_gaps.user: Brigade/battalion geospatial engineers, TAK Server administrators, S6, team leaders loading devices before missions.
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Geospatial cell downloads imagery/OWT/terrain, builds MBTiles/GeoPackage/KMZ packages. 2) Packages are sideloaded to end-user devices or pushed as TAK mission packages, often by hand or USB (sneakernet). 3) Overlays are edited on multiple servers; on reconnection, conflicts are resolved manually or overwritten. 4) Bulk resync after outages saturates SATCOM/MANET links. 5) Updates to 3D terrain are rarely propagated during the operation.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: TAK Server federation and data sync (whole-object, not delta-optimized; RECALL), Immersive Wisdom for low-bandwidth collaboration, Anduril/Palantir edge-to-cloud mesh inside NGC2, manual packaging by geospatial cells.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: No content-aware prioritization or delta encoding for tiles/3D Tiles/overlays across intermittent links; no consistent versioning of the picture across federated servers; edge devices cannot request just what they need.

candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: A content-addressed, priority-aware sync engine for geospatial artifacts (tiles, 3D Tiles, overlays as CRDT documents) exposed as a TAK Server plugin/federation peer and an ATAK/TAKX plugin, with bandwidth-budgeted scheduling per link.
